solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not even Irishman goes to church before start of Yule

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is the stock crossword Irishman

indicators.note: start of tells us to take only the opening letter of the word Yule

explanation.surface: An Irish fellow heads off to church just ahead of Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Something patchy is uneven or irregular in quality, so it is not even.

clue.text: Pattern of work over, aimlessly talk about party

indicators.note: over says the short word for work is turned back to front

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work of music

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the word for party
aimlessly suggests the letters of talk wander into a new order

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A rambling chat at a party after a job is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'over' as finished, but it signals a reversal; 'aimlessly' scrambles talk into LKAT, which 'about' wraps round the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Polka dot is a pattern of evenly spaced round spots on fabric.

clue.text: Soldiers right to work outside

indicators.note: outside says the words for to and work sit around the letter for right

parts.note: taken as written
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Troops are told it is acceptable to labour in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of soldiers, such as a cavalry subdivision.

clue.text: Only item of luggage needed?

parts.note: a bag big enough to carry everything would be the only one you need

explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft travelling bag that can take a great deal.

clue.text: Result of lifts getting heated

parts.note: lifts as a noun, rises or boosts, are ups
heated means hot

explanation.surface: The outcome of elevators overheating.
explanation.definitionFit: An upshot is the final outcome or consequence, a synonym for result.

clue.text: Head holds permit for painting device

indicators.note: holds says the word for head contains the word for permit

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
to permit is to let

explanation.surface: A boss grants a licence for some decorating equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A palette is the board on which an artist mixes paints.

clue.text: Infusion mixed at heel bar

indicators.note: mixed means these letters are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: A herbal drink blended at a shoe-repair counter.
explanation.walkthrough: A heel bar is a British shoe-repair kiosk.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbal tea is made by steeping herbs in hot water, which is an infusion.

clue.text: Attempt to guard goal with it

indicators.note: to guard says the word for attempt surrounds the word for goal protectively

parts.note: an attempt is a try
a goal or aim is an end

explanation.surface: A defender trying to protect the goal mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with it means fashionable and up to date, which is trendy.

clue.text: Deluge with literature, receiving dazzling illumination

parts.note: a deluge is a flood

explanation.surface: Being swamped with books while lit up by a blinding light.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium or building lit by powerful lamps receives a bright, dazzling wash of light.

clue.text: Had a ripping time? What a nuisance!

definitions.meaning: humorously, something just torn has had a ripping time
an exclamation of exasperation when something goes wrong

explanation.definitionFit: That's torn it is a British exclamation meaning things are now spoilt, said here of something literally ripped.

clue.text: Lay in wait and enticed king to get drawn in

indicators.note: the king is pulled into the middle of the word for enticed, a container signal

parts.note: enticed means lured
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone hid in ambush and tempted a monarch to be drawn into a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To lurk is to hide and wait, typically with bad intent, so lurked is lay in wait.

clue.text: Stare, seeing women in space

indicators.note: in places the women letter inside the word for space

parts.note: a space or opening is a gap
W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

explanation.surface: Gazing open-mouthed at women in outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: Gawp is British slang for staring stupidly or open-mouthed.

clue.text: Some savant gardener breaking new ground

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A learned horticulturist is doing pioneering work.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde work is experimental and innovative, pioneering new territory in the arts.

clue.text: Recovering fleece found by valley track

parts.note: to fleece someone is to con or swindle them
a vale is a valley
an animal's scent is the trail a hound follows, its track

explanation.surface: A sheep's coat discovered beside a path through a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A convalescent patient is recuperating, getting better after an illness.

clue.text: Second team in force for red-light district?

parts.note: vice means deputy or second in command, as in vice-captain
a team is a squad

explanation.surface: A reserve side playing within a police force patrolling a sleazy area.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice squad is the police unit dealing with prostitution and similar offences.

clue.text: Doctor has consumed last of flat fish

indicators.note: has consumed says the word for doctor swallows the letter

parts.note: a surgeon is a doctor

indicators.note: last of means take only the final letter of the word flat

explanation.surface: A medic has eaten the remainder of a flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturgeon is a large fish prized for its roe, caviar.

clue.text: Vulgar riches seen in international club?

parts.note: vulgar, meaning coarse or low-class, is common
riches means wealth

explanation.surface: Crude displays of wealth at an exclusive members' club.
explanation.definitionFit: The Commonwealth of Nations is an association of countries, playfully called a club.

clue.text: It reminds me repeatedly not to get drunk

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word me appears twice in a row

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: getting drunk leaves letters reeling, so the word not is jumbled

explanation.surface: A note telling the writer again and again to stay sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get drunk' rearranges NOT as NTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake whose purpose is to bring something to mind.

clue.text: I swayed over edge of road

indicators.note: over suggests the letters keel over and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tottered over the kerb at the side of the street.
explanation.definitionFit: The wayside is the strip beside a road or path.

clue.text: Intended taking flight

parts.note: an intended is a betrothed partner, and one who runs away to marry fits

explanation.definitionFit: An eloper is someone who runs off secretly to marry, a fiancé in flight.

clue.text: Melting ice lolly that could be used as a bribe?

definitions.text: that could be used as a bribe

parts.note: melting ice turns to slush
lolly is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A dripping ice lolly offered as a sweetener to get a favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Slush money is a fund of cash kept for bribery or other illicit payments.

clue.text: Robin dropping end off new pen

indicators.note: new signals that the remaining letters are made anew in a different order
the final letter of the name is lost, a deletion of its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Robin loses the tip of a brand-new fountain pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping end off' leaves ROBI, and 'new' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A biro is a ballpoint pen, named after its inventor László Bíró.

clue.text: Second-class security device for group of buildings

parts.note: B denotes second class or grade
a lock is a security device

explanation.surface: A cheap lock is installed on a housing estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A block is a set of buildings bounded by streets, or one large building divided into units.

clue.text: Cycle at university given precedence — that's an improvement

indicators.note: the university part is put in front of the cycle part, an ordering signal

parts.note: up means at university, as in being up at Oxford
a cycle or revolution is a turn

explanation.surface: A student's bike ride is ranked first, and that is progress.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is an upward change in fortune or figures, an improvement.

clue.text: Tour ended in fall

parts.note: a tour is a trip
something ended is over

explanation.surface: A holiday that came to a close in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip over is to stumble and fall to the ground.

clue.text: Fusion of the rod at a very high temperature

indicators.note: a fusion melts things together into a new form, so these letters are remade

explanation.surface: Melting a metal rod requires enormous heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that is red-hot is glowing from extreme heat.

clue.text: Invite to come over stream to get on

parts.note: a beck is a northern English word for a stream

explanation.surface: Asking someone across a brook so they can carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon is to signal someone to approach, inviting them to come closer.
